meta.title: Why is the road ahead already moving?
meta.summary: Southbound US-101, 15 June 2005. A pocket of slow cars walks back through the section at about 9 mph while the far end is still near 45. For the first ten minutes that far end stays near 40. By fifteen minutes it has slowed to match. FHWA NGSIM trajectories, frozen and labelled.

hero.title: Why is the road ahead already moving?
hero.question: Where should the speed be held when the jam has moving traffic at its front?

sections.headline: Hold the speed while the road ahead is still moving
sections.body:
This story ships as a directed film. Open /stories/where-should-the-speed-be-held/film.

One minute of lane 2, the brake that walks back through the cars, and the morning the window closes. The method, data and schema are at /stories/where-should-the-speed-be-held/method.

dataRefs.label: Lane 2, 240 s to 300 s: the slow cell walks 800 ft back, and the far end stays near 45 mph
dataRefs.note: 100-ft cells on observed trajectories. The featured car is 928, at 840 ft and 15.3 mph.

dataRefs.label: The far end is near 40 mph for the first ten minutes, and near 23 by fifteen
dataRefs.note: Mean speed, lanes 1–5. Upstream is under 500 ft. Downstream is over 1,700 ft.

dataRefs.label: The coarser rule counts a walk on lanes 2 and 3, in the first nine minutes
dataRefs.note: 200-ft by 20-second cells. A faster jump is not counted. Lanes 1, 4 and 5 did not meet the rule.

dataRefs.label: A replay walks the slow cell back and leaves the far end fast; forbidding a harder brake does not
dataRefs.note: The replay slows the cell more than the road did, so its depth is not quoted as a measurement. One minute, one rule.

dataRefs.label: Three cars from the side: a lamp, a gap, and the next lamp later
dataRefs.note: The brake is enlarged. The speeds on the road are measured. Car 928's own acceleration at 240 s is positive.

sources.label: FHWA NGSIM vehicle trajectories, US-101, CC BY-SA 3.0

methodology: Directed film over one frozen evidence pack. FHWA NGSIM trajectories for southbound US-101 on 15 June 2005 are read from the public SODA file. Cell speeds, the pocket's walk and the five-minute bands are arithmetic on those trajectories. A car-following replay of the featured minute is drawn only when the slow cell still walks upstream at about 9 mph and the far end stays in the forties. The opened cars are an illustration.
limitations: One morning, about 2,100 feet, 15 June 2005. Positions are noisy. The entrance and the exit are drawn and not modelled. No variable speed limit was operating, so the film does not claim one would have worked. The film does not say why any particular driver braked.

a11y.alt: Interactive film: cars on a short stretch of US-101 coloured by speed, one car opening into three cars braking, and the slow pocket walking back while the far end is still moving
a11y.reducedMotionNote: With reduced motion, camera moves cut instead of gliding, the illustration shows the braked state without playing, and the beat narration is announced in a live region.

reader.orientation: Southbound US-101, a Wednesday morning in June 2005. You are stopped, and the cars ahead of you are not. This story is about that gap, how it moves, and what the operator can do in the minutes before it closes.

terms.definition: The direction the cars are going. On this picture, toward the far end of the stretch.
A short stretch of slow cars with faster cars on both sides of it.
Back toward the cars that have not reached the slow stretch yet.
Holding drivers to one speed, a little below the open road, so the gaps do not collapse.

labels: the gap is what the next driver sees
each next lamp comes on later
